title: 45yo F Severe Hyponatraemia with Hypovolaemia
chiefComplaint: Vomiting and diarrhoea for 3 days, now confused
background: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, on furosemide and hydrochlorothiazide. Three days of vomiting and watery diarrhoea, drinking only plain water. Today she became confused and had a brief episode of jerking in the taxi. Thiazide plus gastrointestinal losses plus water is the classic route to severe hyponatraemia, and the heart failure makes every litre a judgement call.

exam.finding: Lethargic, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor

investigations.name: Serum osmolality
investigations.report: Hypotonic. This is true hyponatraemia, not pseudohyponatraemia.

investigations.name: Urine sodium
investigations.report: Low urine sodium points to volume depletion, with diuretic effect wearing off.

investigations.name: Urine osmolality
investigations.report: Concentrated urine: ADH is switched on by the low volume. When volume is restored it will switch off.

data.label: Hypertonic 3% saline bolus for the severe symptoms

doseMap.3% saline 150 mL IV over 20 minutes: Aim for a rise of 4 to 6 mmol/L in the first hours. That is enough to reverse cerebral oedema. Then stop the hypertonic saline.

distractors.label: Two litres of normal saline rapidly to fix the shock and the sodium together
distractors.feedback: Once volume is restored, ADH switches off and she passes dilute urine, so sodium can rise 15 mmol/L overnight and cause osmotic demyelination. Treat the brain with a small hypertonic bolus and give volume in measured aliquots.

distractors.label: Restrict fluid to 1 litre a day and recheck tomorrow
distractors.feedback: Fluid restriction is for euvolaemic SIADH. She is confused, has had a seizure-like episode and is dry. Severe symptoms need hypertonic saline now.

data.label: Neurology settles
data.narrative: Sodium rises from 118 to 122 after one bolus. The jerking stops and she answers questions. Four mmol/L was all the hypertonic saline was for.

data.label: Explain to her daughter why you are correcting slowly on purpose (Empathy)
data.narrative: Her daughter wants the number fixed tonight. You explain that the brain has adapted over days and must be allowed to readapt over days. She stops asking for a faster drip and starts writing down the times.

data.choice: Normal saline in 250 mL aliquots, reassess each
data.label: Small isotonic boluses for the hypovolaemia, reassessing each time
actions: Lung ultrasound and auscultation after each aliquot

doseMap.Normal saline 250 mL aliquots: Reassess after each one. Stop when perfusion improves or B-lines appear. Heart failure narrows the margin, it does not remove it.
doseMap.Replace potassium: Potassium chloride 10 mmol/h IV. Potassium raises serum sodium too, so count it in the correction budget.

distractors.label: Withhold all IV fluid because of the heart failure
distractors.feedback: She is hypotensive and dry from three days of losses. Small measured boluses with reassessment are safe and necessary.

distractors.label: Give furosemide to protect her from fluid overload
distractors.feedback: She is volume depleted and diuretics caused this. Furosemide deepens the shock. Stop both diuretics.

data.label: Perfusion restored, then a water diuresis
data.narrative: After 750 mL her pressure is 104/62. Then urine output takes off: 250 mL of dilute urine in an hour. ADH has switched off, and the sodium will now rise on its own.

data.choice: Sodium every 2-4 h, cap the rise at 8 in 24 h
data.label: Watch for overcorrection and clamp it before the limit
actions: Limit the rise to 8 mmol/L in 24 hours
Desmopressin with D5W if the limit is approached

doseMap.Limit the rise to 8 mmol/L in 24 hours: She has three risk factors for osmotic demyelination: sodium below 120, low potassium and a course over several days.
doseMap.Desmopressin with D5W if the limit is ap: Desmopressin 2 mcg IV stops the water diuresis. D5W at 3 mL/kg/h lowers the sodium again if it has already risen too fast.

distractors.label: Aim to bring the sodium to 135 today
distractors.feedback: Correcting by more than 8 to 10 mmol/L in 24 hours risks osmotic demyelination, which appears days later and is often permanent.

distractors.label: Recheck the sodium tomorrow morning
distractors.feedback: A water diuresis can raise sodium by 2 mmol/L an hour. Two to four hourly checks are how overcorrection is caught in time.

data.label: Safe correction
data.narrative: Sodium 125 at 24 hours and 131 at 48. The water diuresis was clamped with desmopressin at hour 10. No neurological deficit. Her thiazide is stopped for good and the heart failure clinic is told why.
